label: Широкий / Узкий
description: Широкий vs узкий: wide/narrow contrasts across genders and everyday scenes.

missions.fullAnalysis: Strategic focus: Masculine nominative agreement. 'Широкий' takes the masculine ending to match 'проспект'. The short sentence isolates the masculine form in a familiar city setting.
Strategic focus: Masculine nominative agreement. 'Узкий' matches masculine 'коридор', and the intensifier underlines the cramped sense. The sentence anchors the form in a concrete indoor space.
Strategic focus: Feminine nominative agreement. 'Широкая' takes the feminine ending to match 'кровать'. The possessive frame keeps the form in an everyday household observation.
Strategic focus: Feminine nominative agreement. 'Узкая' matches feminine 'улица', and the added location gives a vivid old-town image. The sentence reinforces the feminine -ая ending.
Strategic focus: Neuter nominative agreement. 'Широкое' takes the neuter ending to match 'окно'. The spatial frame shows the learner switching endings inside a room description.
Strategic focus: Neuter nominative agreement. 'Узкое' matches neuter 'кресло', and the second adjective reinforces the cramped sense. The sentence keeps the neuter -ое ending in a practical comment.
Strategic focus: Plural nominative agreement. 'Широкие' takes the plural ending to match 'дороги'. The added 'поля' broadens the open-space image around the plural form.
Strategic focus: Plural nominative agreement. 'Узкие' matches plural 'плечи' in a common description of build. The possessive frame grounds the plural -ие ending in real speech.

missions.phrase: Этот мост широкий, а тот узкий.
missions.fullAnalysis: Strategic focus: Direct contrast across two masculine nouns. 'Широкий' and 'узкий' both agree with 'мост', set off by the demonstratives 'этот' and 'тот'. The comma-joined clauses make the wide-versus-narrow opposition explicit.

Strategic focus: Comparative form of широкий. 'Шире' is the irregular comparative meaning wider, used with the genitive 'той' for comparison. The sentence shows the pair moving into a comparative judgment.
